original_card.question: Does one selected supplier obligation follow from its actual source-bound checks?
methods: Trace one hypothesis through the source, checker and complete caller.
Construct one semantically invalid but superficially well-formed fixture and test rejection.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the current sources and one obligation; the historical owner audit is an example, not evidence of a current bug.

first_step.inspect: Identify why the timing-only omission passes but the full production controller still rejects it.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one current supplier obligation and trace whether its acceptance depends on an independent check.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Closing a current acceptance gap or proof obligation strengthens reliability even without changing kappa.
allowed_variations: Audit one named current condition using a new semantic counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Reporting the historical timing-only diagnostic as a new current acceptance bug.

actual_scope: Mutant coverage of one selected-supplier checker: the frozen PR1087 code/audit_allcold.py (sha256 1467a2ac...) run in-process on the selected #1094 hosted template archived in research/community-frontier1094-audit/selected-replay.tar.gz. For the 15 shipped mutation controls, 35 new targeted semantic mutants and a 111-field one-at-a-time census, record the rejecting line; check the template owner map against the frozen data/OWNERS.json.gz.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether one selected supplier obligation follows from its actual checks. This narrows it to the controller/owner audit of the selected final stage and asks which of its predicates are exercised by any negative control, then supplies a semantic counterexample for each unexercised one.
bottleneck_link: Side result for reliability: no kappa change. It shows that the selected final stage's owner/window/cell/schedule predicates each reject a targeted invalid fixture, and records the one cross-stage link (template owners = frozen OWNERS) that no stage checked.
stop_rule: Stop at the first accepted semantically consequential mutant (report it) or when every reachable assert statement in audit() has a rejecting mutant; unreachable ones are explained.
evidence: verify.py: 15/15 shipped controls rejected, first reaching 8 of the 42 lines with an assert; 34/35 new mutants rejected, reaching 20 more (the field census 6 more) (idle window both sides, cross-call cell overlap, pending-prefix gap, schedule order/retiming, pooled-slot binding); accepted: pooled-slot time (line 172 omits it), 15 fields audit() never reads (no post-emit reader by text search) and 3 partial checks; template pooled_slots == frozen OWNERS (69,120 roles) and owner_map_sha256 names it; 8 asserts unreachable by template mutation, each explained. Identical EXPECTED.json on CPython 3.10/3.12/3.14.
